title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
abstract: arXiv:2611.27741v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have endowed multimodal agents with increasingly strong visual perception and long-horizon reasoning capabilities, making VLM-based autonomous game playing feasible. Existing game benchmarks primarily evaluate whether an agent can select appropriate actions from the current visual state across different scenarios and games. However, most of them adopt a step-by-step interaction paradigm where the current visual observation is sent to the agent before each action. In practical deployment, this paradigm introduces two fundamental limitations: the game loop must wait for model inference, making real-time interaction impractical, and repeated VLM calls incur substantial cost. translated_title: 视觉语言模型能否合成可执行的游戏程序？
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）的最新进展赋予多模态智能体日益强大的视觉感知和长程推理能力，使得基于VLM的自主游戏成为可能。现有的游戏基准主要评估智能体能否在不同场景和游戏中根据当前视觉状态选择合适的动作。然而，它们大多采用逐步交互范式，即在每个动作执行前将当前视觉观察发送给智能体。在实际部署中，这种范式引入了两个根本性限制：游戏循环必须等待模型推理，使得实时交互难以实现；同时重复调用VLM会带来高昂的成本。因此，我们提出了PlayScriptBench，一个基于脚本的游戏基准，用于评估VLM能否根据游戏状态合成可执行的游戏程序。这一设置同时评估了视觉定位、理解等多方面能力。
tldr: 该论文提出了PlayScriptBench基准，评估视觉语言模型能否从游戏状态直接合成可执行的游戏程序，以克服逐步交互范式在实时性和调用成本方面的根本局限。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes PlayScriptBench, a script-based game benchmark that evaluates whether vision-language models can synthesize executable game-playing programs from game states, overcoming the real-time and cost limitations of the step-by-step interaction paradigm.
